'''David D. Awschalom''' (born 1956 in [[Baton Rouge, Louisiana]], United States)<ref name=AAAS>{{cite web|title=Book of Members, 1780-2010: Chapter A|url=http://www.amacad.org/publications/BookofMembers/ChapterA.pdf|publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences|accessdate=28 April 2011}}</ref> is an American [[condensed matter physics|condensed matter]] experimental [[physicist]]. He is best known for his work in [[spintronics]] in [[semiconductors]].

Awschalom graduated from the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]] with a B.Sc. in physics. He received a Ph.D. in experimental physics from [[Cornell University]].<ref name="UCSBpage">{{cite web|url=http://awsch-web.physics.ucsb.edu/members/awschalom/index.php|title=David Awschalom|work=The Awschalom Group|publisher=University of California, Santa Barbara|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110725080356/http://awsch-web.physics.ucsb.edu/members/awschalom/index.php|archivedate=25 July 2011|accessdate=28 April 2011}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://pme.uchicago.edu/awschalomlab/people/david_awschalom/|title=David Awschalom - People - Awschalom Group - Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering|website=pme.uchicago.edu|access-date=2019-10-27}}</ref> He is the director of the Chicago Quantum Exchange<ref>{{cite web |title=David Awschalom Bio Page |url=https://chicagoquantum.org/people/david-awschalom |website=Chicago Quantum Exchange |access-date=11 May 2022}}</ref> and a Liew Family Professor in Molecular Engineering at the [[University of Chicago]]'s Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering (PME).<ref name=":0" /> He previously served as the director of the [[California Nanosystems Institute]] and was a professor in the [[UC Santa Barbara Physics Department|physics department]] at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]] as well as an associated faculty member in the department of electrical and computer engineering. He has a [[Hirsch number]] of 119.

== Awards and honors ==
* elected [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]] (1992)<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=A&year=&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive|publisher=APS|accessdate=18 June 2020}} </ref>
* [[Buckley Prize|Oliver E. Buckley Prize]] by the [[American Physical Society]] (2005)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm|title=2018 Stanley Corrsin Award Recipient|website=www.aps.org|language=en|access-date=2019-10-27}}</ref>
* Agilent [[Europhysics Prize]] by the [[European Physical Society]] (2005)<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.physics.rutgers.edu/~kotliar/agitech.html|title=[ EPS ]|website=www.physics.rutgers.edu|access-date=2019-10-27}}</ref>
* elected fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (2006)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.amacad.org/person/david-d-awschalom|title=David D. Awschalom|website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences|language=en|access-date=2019-10-27}}</ref>
* elected member of [[National Academy of Sciences]] (2007)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/david-d-awschalom-iac4ct/|title=David Awschalom|website=www.nasonline.org|access-date=2019-10-27}}</ref>
* Turnbull Lectureship Award from the [[Materials Research Society]] (2010)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mrs.org/turnbull|title=David Turnbull Lectureship|website=www.mrs.org|access-date=2019-10-27|archive-date=April 5, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110405102447/https://www.mrs.org/turnbull|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* elected member of [[National Academy of Engineering]] (2011)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nae.edu/42023/Professor-David-D-Awschalom|title=Professor David D. Awschalom|website=NAE Website|access-date=2019-10-27}}</ref>
